passages.title: Launch: the SmartDesk 2
passages.text:
Hartley Group announces the launch of the SmartDesk 2, available from 12 September. The product is designed for small businesses and features automatic height adjustment.

“We wanted to make ergonomic furniture affordable,” said CEO Laura Bennett. The launch follows eighteen months of development and testing with more than 200 customers.

the SmartDesk 2 will be priced at $499. It will be available through the company website and selected retail partners.

passages.title: Launch: the EcoPack Pro
passages.text:
Hartley Group announces the launch of the EcoPack Pro, available from 3 October. The product is designed for food retailers and features fully compostable packaging.

“Sustainability should not mean higher costs,” said CEO Laura Bennett. The launch follows eighteen months of development and testing with more than 200 customers.

the EcoPack Pro will be priced at $0.35 per unit. It will be available through the company website and selected retail partners.

passages.title: Launch: the FlowPay app
passages.text:

the FlowPay app will be priced at $9.99 per month. It will be available through the company website and selected retail partners.

passages.title: Market research: the UK home-office furniture market
passages.text:
Market research summary: the UK home-office furniture market

We surveyed 1,200 consumers in the target segment. The key finding is that price is the most important factor. The strongest competitor is WorkSpace Direct, which has a 24% market share.

Based on these results, we recommend that the company launch a mid-priced range. This would allow us to differentiate our offer and address the most important customer priorities.

A full report with detailed charts is available on the shared drive.

Based on these results, we recommend that the company develop an open API. This would allow us to differentiate our offer and address the most important customer priorities.

A full report with detailed charts is available on the shared drive.

passages.title: Sustainability report: Hartley Group
passages.text:
Hartley Group has reduced its operational emissions by 32% since 2019, according to its latest sustainability report. Renewable sources now account for 61% of the company’s electricity use.

The company has committed to reaching net zero by 2040 and plans to invest $18 million in low-carbon technology over the next five years. However, the report acknowledges that decarbonizing the supply chain remains the most difficult challenge.

“We have made genuine progress, but the next phase will require closer collaboration with suppliers and customers,” said the sustainability director.

passages.title: Sustainability report: Northwind Logistics
passages.text:
Northwind Logistics has reduced its operational emissions by 27% since 2019, according to its latest sustainability report. Renewable sources now account for 48% of the company’s electricity use.

The company has committed to reaching net zero by 2035 and plans to invest $42 million in low-carbon technology over the next five years. However, the report acknowledges that replacing the diesel fleet remains the most difficult challenge.

“We have made genuine progress, but the next phase will require closer collaboration with suppliers and customers,” said the sustainability director.

passages.title: Sustainability report: Lumen Retail
passages.text:
Lumen Retail has reduced its operational emissions by 19% since 2019, according to its latest sustainability report. Renewable sources now account for 73% of the company’s electricity use.

The company has committed to reaching net zero by 2045 and plans to invest $9 million in low-carbon technology over the next five years. However, the report acknowledges that reducing packaging waste remains the most difficult challenge.

“We have made genuine progress, but the next phase will require closer collaboration with suppliers and customers,” said the sustainability director.
